legend: VERIFIED = read on an official docs/pricing page on 2026-10-19. UNVERIFIED = third-party source or inferred; console URLs are best-known paths and may redirect.

providers.name: Groq
providers.free_tier: Free plan, per model. LLMs gpt-oss-120b/20b and qwen/qwen3.8-27b: 30 RPM, 1K RPD, 8K TPM, 200K TPD. whisper-large-v3(-turbo): 20 RPM, 2K RPD, 7.2K audio-sec/hour, 28.8K audio-sec/day. Your account's own numbers are at console.groq.com/settings/limits.
providers.notes: The model list is VERIFIED. The rate-limit page says its table shows 'base limits for the Developer plan'; the numbers match the usual free-plan values, but check them in the console (UNVERIFIED that they are the free values). Limits for llama-3.x on the free plan were not shown. Older IDs like mixtral, gemma2 and llama3-70b-8192 are gone. OpenAI-compatible base URL: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1.

providers.name: Google AI Studio (Gemini API)
providers.free_tier: Free tier for each project, with no billing account needed. Per-model RPM/TPM/RPD are no longer published on the rate-limits page; see them under your project in AI Studio. Third-party reports of the Flash free tier range from about 5-15 RPM and 20-1,500 RPD, and limits were cut in Dec 2025 and Apr 2026 (UNVERIFIED). Free-tier prompts may be used to improve Google products.
free_models: gemma-4 (free; exact ID not listed on the pricing page)
providers.notes: The free/paid split by model is VERIFIED from the pricing page. These have NO free tier: gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-4-argon, image models (gemini-*-image, nano-banana), Veo and Lyria. gemini-2.0-flash-lite was shut down on 2026-06-01 (third-party). The SDKs read GEMINI_API_KEY, with GOOGLE_API_KEY as a fallback.

providers.name: Mistral AI (La Plateforme / Studio)
providers.free_tier: Free 'Experiment' plan, called 'Free mode' in the current docs. No card, but the help center says a verified phone number is required (one per plan). Rate limits are per model and shown in the console. Third-party figures are about 1 req/s, 500K TPM and 1B tokens/month per model (UNVERIFIED and conflicting). Requests on the free plan may be used for training.
providers.notes: Experiment/Free mode covers essentially all API models. The models page does not show the -latest aliases, so the aliases above are UNVERIFIED. Prefer them over pinned IDs, because many pinned IDs retired in 2026: mistral-small-2506, open-mistral-nemo-2407, mistral-large-2411, magistral-small-2509, devstral-2512, and mistral-medium-2508 (retired 2026-08-31). Mistral agreed to acquire Koyeb in Feb 2026.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.free_tier: :free model variants: 20 RPM; 50 requests/day if you have bought less than $10 of credits in total, 1,000 requests/day after buying $10 or more (one-time, lifetime).
providers.notes: Free model list is VERIFIED live from GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on 2026-10-19. It changes often, so the app should fetch it at runtime and filter IDs ending in ':free'. The once-popular deepseek, llama and qwen :free variants are NOT currently listed. Each API key can have its own credit limit as a spend guard.

providers.name: Cloudflare (Workers, Workers AI, R2, D1, KV, Pages)
providers.free_tier: Workers: 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU per invocation; static asset requests are free and unlimited. Workers AI: 10,000 Neurons/day, then $0.011 per 1K Neurons, which needs Workers Paid. KV: 100K reads/day, 1K writes/deletes/lists per day, 1 GB. D1: 5M rows read/day, 100K rows written/day, 5 GB total. R2: 10 GB-month, 1M Class A and 10M Class B ops per month, free egress (Standard storage class only). Pages: 500 builds/month, 1 concurrent build (20 min timeout), 20,000 files per site, 25 MiB per file, 100 custom domains per project. Pages Functions count against the Workers quota. Daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC.
providers.notes: Limits and model IDs are VERIFIED (IDs from developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/llms.txt). Workers AI usage counts against the daily Neuron allowance, and big models use Neurons quickly. Enabling R2 asks for a payment method on first use even for the free tier (third-party guides; UNVERIFIED on official docs), so card_required is effectively true for R2 only. R2 S3 keys are created at https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/r2/api-tokens. There is no hard spending cap; billing notifications are at Notifications > Billing > Usage-based billing.

providers.name: NVIDIA build.nvidia.com (NIM API)
providers.free_tier: Free hosted API for development and prototyping only, about 40 RPM (shared across models per some reports; varies by model and load). NVIDIA forum moderators say rate-limit increases are not granted on this tier. The old signup credits (1,000-5,000) were reportedly phased out.
providers.notes: UNVERIFIED: build.nvidia.com was not fetched directly; the facts come from NVIDIA forum threads and third-party guides. The terms say the free tier is not for production, and inputs may be logged. OpenAI-compatible base URL: https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1, model list at GET /v1/models. There is no billing because there is no paid tier on build.nvidia.com.

providers.name: Cohere
providers.free_tier: Trial key: 1,000 API calls/month across all endpoints. Chat 20 req/min, Embed 2,000 inputs/min, Rerank 10 req/min, Embed images 5 inputs/min, Tokenize 100 req/min, other endpoints 500 req/min. Trial keys are for non-commercial use.
providers.notes: VERIFIED. The old aliases command-r, command-r-plus, command and command-light are retired. The official SDK reads CO_API_KEY.

providers.name: SambaNova Cloud
providers.free_tier: Free Tier (no payment method on the account): 20 RPM, 20 RPD and 200,000 tokens/day per model. Developer Tier (payment method added): 60-240 RPM, 12K-48K RPD, capped at 20M tokens/day across all models.
providers.notes: Limits are VERIFIED. A free tier of 20 requests/day per model is very small. Third-party sources mention a $5 starter credit when you add a card (UNVERIFIED). Console URLs are UNVERIFIED. OpenAI-compatible base URL: https://api.sambanova.ai/v1.

providers.name: Z.AI (Zhipu GLM)
providers.free_tier: GLM Flash models are free: $0 input, cached input and output. The official page gives no rate limits; third parties report about 1 req/s (concurrency 1) and around 1,000 req/day (UNVERIFIED).
providers.notes: The free model list is VERIFIED from the official pricing page. Flagship GLM-5.x models are paid. OpenAI-compatible base URL: https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4. Key and billing URLs are UNVERIFIED. China mainland users go to open.bigmodel.cn instead.

providers.name: Cerebras Inference
providers.free_tier: CHANGED: there is no longer a permanent free tier. The 'Free Trial' gives $5 of credits once you add a verified payment method, and the credits expire after 30 days. Trial limits per model: 5 RPM, 30K uncached / 90K total TPM, 1M tokens/hour, 1M tokens/day. Paid access starts at $10.
providers.notes: VERIFIED from official docs. API and Playground stay inactive until a card is added, and access stops when the $5 runs out. Treat Cerebras as a short trial, not a permanent free provider. The key URL path is UNVERIFIED. Base URL: https://api.cerebras.ai/v1.

providers.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (Always Free)
providers.free_tier: Ampere A1: 1,500 OCPU-hours and 9,000 GB-hours per month, which works out to 2 OCPU and 12 GB RAM. Up to 2 instances (2 OCPUs total), home region only. AMD VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro: up to 2 instances, each 1/8 OCPU (burstable), 1 GB RAM, 50 Mbps. Autonomous AI Database: 2 databases, each 1 OCPU, 20 GB storage, 20 sessions. Block Volume: 200 GB total for boot and block volumes, 5 backups. Object Storage: 20 GB and 50K API requests/month. Plus a $300 / 30-day trial at signup.
providers.notes: CHANGED: the A1 limit is now 2 OCPU / 12 GB (1,500 OCPU-h / 9,000 GB-h), NOT the older 4 OCPU / 24 GB (3,000 OCPU-h / 18,000 GB-h) VERIFIED on official docs. Idle instances can be reclaimed: over 7 days, 95th-percentile CPU, network and (A1 only) memory all below 20%. 'Out of host capacity' errors are common. A card is required for identity verification at signup. The API uses request signing (a key pair uploaded under the user's API keys), not a bearer token.

providers.name: Google Cloud (Cloud Run, Compute Engine e2-micro, Firestore, GCS)
providers.free_tier: Cloud Run (request-based): 2M requests, 180,000 vCPU-seconds, 360,000 GiB-seconds, 1 GB North America egress per month. Compute Engine: 1 non-preemptible e2-micro in us-west1, us-central1 or us-east1, 30 GB-month standard persistent disk, 1 GB egress. Firestore: 1 GiB storage, 50K reads, 20K writes and 20K deletes per day per project, 10 GiB egress/month. Cloud Storage: 5 GB-month regional storage (US regions only), 5K Class A ops, 50K Class B ops, 100 GB egress. Plus a $300 / 90-day welcome credit.
providers.notes: VERIFIED. The Free Tier needs a billing account, which needs a card or other payment method ($0-1 temporary hold). Budgets only send alerts; they do not cap spending. Docs moved to docs.cloud.google.com.

providers.name: AWS DynamoDB
providers.free_tier: Each month, per Region: 25 GB storage, 25 WCU and 25 RCU provisioned (Standard table class, roughly 200M requests/month), 25 rWCU for global tables, 2.5M Streams reads, 1 GB data transfer out (15 GB in the first 12 months). Also up to $200 of AWS Free Tier credits for 6 months for new accounts.
providers.notes: Mostly VERIFIED. The DynamoDB allowance is the always-free part, but the free tier applies to provisioned capacity only; on-demand mode is billed. AWS moved new accounts to a credit-based free plan (up to $200 / 6 months) in July 2025; the pricing page mentions the credits but not the change date (UNVERIFIED detail). A card is required at signup. Prefer IAM users or roles with least privilege.

providers.name: Supabase
providers.free_tier: 2 active projects (paused ones do not count). Per project: 500 MB database (shared CPU, 500 MB RAM), 1 GB file storage (50 MB max upload), 5 GB egress + 5 GB cached egress, 50,000 MAU, 500K Edge Function invocations. Projects pause after 1 week of inactivity.
providers.notes: Limits are VERIFIED. The pricing page does not say whether a card is needed; the free plan is widely known to need no card (UNVERIFIED on page). Supabase is moving from anon/service_role JWT keys to sb_publishable_ / sb_secret_ keys, so store both kinds. The app may need a keep-alive to prevent the 7-day pause.

providers.name: Neon (serverless Postgres)
providers.free_tier: Up to 100 projects. Per project: 1 GB storage (20 GB total across projects), 100 CU-hours/month, 5 GB egress, 10 branches. Scale-to-zero after 5 min of inactivity is always on.
providers.notes: VERIFIED (pricing page says 'no credit card required'). The domain moved to neon.com. Neon was acquired by Databricks in 2025.

providers.name: Turso (libSQL)
providers.key_url: https://app.turso.tech/ (Settings > API Tokens for the platform token; per-database tokens via `turso db tokens create <db>`)
providers.free_tier: 100 databases, 5 GB storage, 500M rows read/month, 10M rows written/month, 3 GB syncs/month.
providers.notes: VERIFIED ('no credit card required').

providers.name: MongoDB Atlas
providers.free_tier: M0 Free cluster: 512 MB storage, shared RAM/vCPU, up to 100 ops/sec, no backups, no data-transfer charges. One M0 per project.
providers.notes: Storage and ops limits are VERIFIED. The connection limit (about 500), one-M0-per-project rule and no-card signup are from memory/docs (UNVERIFIED this session). The old Serverless and M2/M5 tiers were replaced by Flex ($0.011/h, max $30/mo, 5 GB). Atlas API keys are being replaced by Service Accounts (OAuth client credentials). Database user credentials go in MONGODB_URI.

providers.name: Upstash (Redis, QStash; Kafka discontinued)
providers.free_tier: Redis: 500K commands/month, 250 MB data, 10 GB bandwidth/month (the page says 1 free database in the table but 'up to 10' in the FAQ). QStash: 1,000 messages/day, 50 GB bandwidth, 1 MB max message. Kafka: DISCONTINUED.
providers.notes: Upstash Kafka was deprecated 2024-09-11, closed to new users, and discontinued 2025-03-11. Upstash recommends QStash/Workflow instead, so remove Kafka from the spec. Redis and QStash limits are VERIFIED. Adding a card moves a database to pay-as-you-go automatically.

providers.name: IBM Cloudant
providers.free_tier: Lite plan: 1 GB storage (no extra storage), 20 reads/s, 10 writes/s, 5 global queries/s, not scalable. One Lite instance per IBM Cloud account.
providers.notes: Lite limits are VERIFIED. Card requirement is UNVERIFIED: IBM Cloud has required a card for identity verification for new accounts since about 2023. Lite instances may be deleted after a period of inactivity (UNVERIFIED). Per-instance service credentials are also created under the Cloudant instance > Service credentials.

providers.name: Backblaze B2
providers.free_tier: First 10 GB of storage free. Free egress up to 3x average monthly storage, then $0.01/GB. Class A/B/C calls are free for pay-as-you-go accounts; Class D gets 2,500/day free, then $0.004 per 10K.
providers.notes: Pricing is VERIFIED. Classic B2 has always offered 10 GB without a card; the page does not say (card status UNVERIFIED). B2 has real spending caps (Caps & Alerts), which are better than alerts only. S3-compatible endpoint format: s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com.

providers.name: Koyeb
providers.free_tier: NO free compute tier for new signups. The pricing page starts at Pro ($29/mo plus compute, including $10 of compute). The only free item is a Serverless Postgres 'Free 5h' instance (0.25 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 1 GB storage). Existing orgs keep the old free web service (512 MB RAM, 0.1 vCPU, Frankfurt/Washington, scale-to-zero).
providers.notes: DISCONTINUED for new users: after Mistral AI agreed to acquire Koyeb (announced 2026-02-17), Koyeb said new users can only sign up for Pro and above (VERIFIED from the pricing page and Koyeb blog). A competitor reports a $29 card pre-authorization (UNVERIFIED). Drop Koyeb as a free host.

providers.name: Vercel
providers.free_tier: Hobby, per month: 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 10 GB Fast Origin Transfer, 1M CDN requests, 1M function invocations, 4 active-CPU hours, 360 GB-hours provisioned memory, 5K image transformations. 200 projects, 100 deployments/day, 300 s max function duration, 1 hour of runtime logs. Over the limit, the feature pauses until 30 days pass.
providers.notes: VERIFIED (docs updated 2026-09-14). Hobby is for non-commercial personal use only. Spend Management is not available on Hobby, but it has no overage billing anyway. The AI Gateway gives free users $5 of credits every 30 days.

providers.name: Netlify
providers.free_tier: CHANGED to credit-based pricing. The Free plan has 300 credits (understood to be per month). Costs: production deploy 15 credits, bandwidth 20 credits/GB, compute 10 credits/GB-hour, web requests 2 credits per 10K, AI inference varies. So 300 credits is about 15 GB of bandwidth, or 20 deploys.
providers.notes: The credit model is VERIFIED. Monthly reset, behavior when credits run out (sites reportedly pause until the next cycle) and card status are UNVERIFIED; the pricing page does not say. The old allowance (100 GB bandwidth, 300 build minutes) no longer applies to new accounts.

providers.name: GitHub
providers.free_tier: GitHub Free: unlimited public/private repos. Actions: free standard runners for public repos; 2,000 min/month for private repos. 500 MB artifact + Packages storage (shared), 10 GB Actions cache per repo. GitHub Pages is free for public repos.
providers.notes: VERIFIED. Larger runners are always billed. Use fine-grained PATs; the classic token page is https://github.com/settings/tokens. Budgets docs: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/how-tos/set-up-budgets.

providers.name: Tailscale
providers.free_tier: Personal plan (free forever, non-commercial): up to 6 users, unlimited user devices, 50 tagged resources, 1,000 ephemeral-minutes/month, 3 ACL groups, Tailscale SSH on up to 5 hosts. Includes subnet routers, exit nodes, MagicDNS and ACLs.
providers.notes: Limits are VERIFIED. CHANGED: the old '3 users / 100 devices' figure is out of date. The pricing page does not mention a card; signup uses an SSO identity provider and needs no card (UNVERIFIED). API keys expire (max 90 days), so prefer an OAuth client for long-lived automation.

providers.name: Pi-hole (v6 REST API)
providers.key_url: http://pi.hole/admin/settings/api (local web UI: Settings > Web interface / API > 'Configure app password')
providers.free_tier: Self-hosted and free (open source).
providers.notes: v6 auth (VERIFIED): POST /api/auth with {"password": "<password or app password>"} (plus "totp" if 2FA is on). The reply contains session.sid, session.csrf and session.validity (seconds). Send the SID in the X-FTL-SID header (or as the ?sid= parameter); cookie auth also needs X-FTL-CSRF. Each request extends the session, and idle sessions expire. DELETE /api/auth logs out (204). Logins are rate-limited (429) and concurrent sessions are capped, so reuse and close sessions. App passwords work with 2FA. The v5 api.php?auth=<token> scheme is gone.
